U.S. Army boosts funding for new Kentucky TNT plant
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:26:37 UTC
18:26:37 KST

- The U.S. Army modified its TNT production facility contract with Paligen Aerospace & Defense, bringing the total value to $435 million.
- The Kentucky facility will be the first domestic TNT production site in the United States since the 1980s, targeted for completion around 2027.
The U.S. Army has ordered $30.8 million in additional work under a contract to build a domestic factory to manufacture TNT in Kentucky, bringing the deal’s total value to $435 million.
The modification, awarded to Paligen Aerospace & Defense LLC, based in Tampa, Florida, covers design, construction and commissioning work on the facility. Army Contracting Command in Rock Island, Illinois, is managing the contract, which is expected to run through February 15, 2029.
TNT is the primary explosive used to fill 155mm artillery shells, along with a range of other munitions from artillery rounds to aircraft bombs. The Army has described the facility as the first domestic TNT production site in the United States since the 1980s, when the Radford Army Ammunition Plant in Virginia halted TNT manufacturing. The Army originally awarded the $435 million contract in November 2024 to Paligen’s predecessor company, then known as REPKON USA, without competitive bidding.
The facility is being built at a commercial site in Graham, Kentucky. According to Paligen, the plant is designed to use automation, digitization and a new waste neutralization process, with construction and full operation targeted within 36 months of the original award, putting completion around early 2027. The award was funded in part through the 2024 Ukraine Supplemental appropriation.
Paligen Technologies, the parent company formed when REPKON USA rebranded in March 2026, has expanded significantly since the TNT contract was first awarded. The company acquired a 38-acre manufacturing facility in Garland, Texas, from General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems in March 2025, along with defense engineering firm McCormick Stevenson Corporation. Paligen now employs more than 400 people across facilities in Florida, Kentucky and Texas.
The push to rebuild domestic TNT capacity has gained added urgency since October 2025, when an explosion destroyed an Accurate Energetic Systems facility in Humphreys County, Tennessee, which had been supplying TNT to the Pentagon. The loss of that plant left the Army without any operating domestic TNT source while the Kentucky facility remains under construction.
The Army’s investment in domestic TNT production has come as the service has separately struggled to rebuild its broader artillery shell manufacturing base. ProPublica reported that General Dynamics failed to get two 155mm shell production lines in Mesquite, Texas, operating as planned before the Army shut the effort down, even as the company continued receiving other Army contracts totaling $2.5 billion since that shutdown.

Taiwan’s TSMC says 3DFabric can boost AI computing
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:25:56 UTC
18:25:56 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — TSMC’s 3DFabric platform can increase AI computing density and memory bandwidth while improving power delivery and cooling, TSMC Advanced Packaging R&D Director Chen Yen-ming (陳燕銘) said Tuesday.
Speaking at the Heterogeneous Integration Summit ahead of SEMICON Taiwan, Chen said AI is pushing chipmakers to find new ways to fit more computing power into smaller spaces, per CNA. He said better chip design alone is not enough, and companies also need to improve how chips are connected, powered, and cooled.
Chen said AI computing performance is improving fivefold each year, while AI models are also processing several times more tokens, or units of data. He said TSMC’s 3DFabric platform brings together several technologies, including CoWoS advanced packaging, to fit more computing power and memory into AI systems while improving data transfer and cooling.
For System on Integrated Chips, Chen said TSMC plans to reduce the connection spacing between parts of its A14 chips to 4.5 micrometers by 2029. TSMC is also applying its technology to high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI systems, with HBM4 base dies made using its N12 process expected to cut power consumption by more than 45% and increase bandwidth 2.5 times, CNA reported.
Chen said TSMC is also developing its Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE), which connects electronic and optical components to move data more efficiently. TSMC plans to move COUPE closer to the main chip by placing it on an interposer, which Chen said can further improve power efficiency and reduce delays.
CoWoS packaging will also allow TSMC to fit more components into a single package as package sizes grow, Chen said. He said TSMC expects a CoWoS package that can support 24 HBM stacks and exceed 14 times the size of a standard reticle by 2029, while the number of AI computing transistors in a single package is projected to grow more than 48-fold from 2024 to 2029 and HBM bandwidth to increase 34-fold.

Iran, Kyrgyzstan review proposal for joint oil refinery construction
Unknown

Iran, Kyrgyzstan review proposal for joint oil refinery construction
TEHRAN – In a significant move toward deepening energy and economic ties, Iran and Kyrgyzstan have agreed to jointly review a proposal for the construction of an oil refinery in Kyrgyzstan. The announcement came on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and Shanghai-Plus summit held in Kyrgyzstan on Monday.
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, who met with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on the summit's margins, confirmed that Tehran has reviewed the proposal positively and agreed to its principle. "Kyrgyzstan's proposal for the joint construction of a refinery in this country has been reviewed positively, and Iran agrees with the principle of this proposal," Pezeshkian stated.
Under the proposed framework, Iran would supply the crude oil required for the refinery, while the resulting petroleum products would be divided between the two nations. The Iranian president described this model of cooperation as a timely opportunity to elevate the level of economic and energy collaboration between the two countries.
The proposal comes at a critical juncture, as energy cooperation has been a central pillar of bilateral relations in recent years. Kyrgyzstan, which currently depends heavily on imports to meet its domestic oil and petroleum product needs, stands to benefit significantly from domestic refining capacity. If finalized, the partnership could expand beyond simple oil and product trade into joint investment, refining operations, technical and engineering services, and the marketing of petroleum products.
President Japarov welcomed the expansion of economic and energy cooperation with Iran and extended an invitation to capable Iranian companies active in oil exploration to bring their expertise to Kyrgyzstan. This invitation is expected to pave the way for a greater Iranian corporate presence in Kyrgyzstan's oil projects and the utilization of Iranian technical and engineering capabilities across various sectors of the Central Asian nation's petroleum industry.
Expanding bilateral economic ties
The refinery proposal is part of a broader push to strengthen economic relations between the two countries. In early August, Iran's Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade, Seyyed Mohammad Atabak, met with Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Economy and Commerce, Sydykov Bakyt Tolomushevich. During that meeting, both sides emphasized the development of trade exchanges, joint investment, and the expansion of cooperation in industry, mining, energy, transport, and free zones.
The two ministers underscored the vast capacities for economic cooperation and stressed the importance of advancing trade and investment within the framework of regional agreements, including the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. They also discussed joint production for export to third-country markets, increased collaboration in the export of knowledge-based products, pharmaceuticals, and medical equipment, as well as expanded cooperation between free zones.
Mining, energy, and transit cooperation
In the mining and energy sector, Kyrgyzstan's mineral wealth was a key topic. Iran announced its readiness to cooperate in exploration, extraction, processing, provision of technical and engineering services, modernization of mining industries, and the transfer of technical knowledge.
On the transport and transit front, the two sides emphasized the activation of the Bandar Abbas–Osh railway route, the establishment of direct flights, the reduction of transit costs, and the completion of regional corridors. They also highlighted the importance of participating in China's "Belt and Road" initiative and utilizing Iran's strategic transit position to connect Kyrgyzstan to regional and international markets.
Banking and financial infrastructure
To facilitate this expanding economic partnership, both countries agreed on the development of banking, logistics, and transport infrastructure. Other key agreements included holding a joint banking committee, utilizing national currencies in bilateral transactions, establishing joint investment funds, and employing modern financing methods.
As Iran and Kyrgyzstan continue to build on their growing partnership, the proposed joint oil refinery stands as a potential flagship project—one that could redefine the contours of their economic and energy cooperation for years to come.

More than 100 firefighters were deployed, and no one was injured. The blaze damaged about 1,500 square meters of the building, destroying the first floor and damaging about one-third of the second floor.
Zhinan Temple Chair Kao Chao-wen (高超文) said the rebuilding project is expected to take at least three years and cost more than NT$100 million (US$3.16 million). Kao said the temple has begun cataloging the damage, filing insurance claims, and raising funds for the restoration, per CNA.
Kao said a fire investigation determined that faulty electrical wiring caused the blaze. The fire spread rapidly after reaching wooden decorative panels in the upper part of the hall, he said. The temple will carefully assess damaged religious artifacts and decorations before deciding what can be restored and what must be replaced.
Undamaged bronze statues blackened by smoke will be cleaned, while damaged statues will be repaired by craftspeople. Items that were destroyed will be recreated, Kao said. The temple will also assess damage to carved decorations, paintings, and roof tiles.
“We will strive to present the original appearance and preserve the ancient style,” Kao said, adding that the goal is for the restored hall to retain the appearance familiar to generations of worshippers. Because the project involves traditional sculpture and other specialized craftsmanship, architects and skilled artisans will be consulted on the design and restoration, he said.
Kao said structural engineers have inspected the building and determined that its main structure remains suitable for restoration, with reinforcement to be carried out where necessary. The temple plans to install fire-resistant materials and establish an upgraded fire protection system as part of the reconstruction.
The Taipei City Government has said it will establish a cross-departmental task force to assist with restoration, involving the Department of Civil Affairs, Fire Department, Department of Cultural Affairs, and other agencies. Although Lingxiao Hall is not designated a historic site, both central government and municipal officials have expressed concern over the damage.
The hall was constructed from 1963 to 1966, according to Zhinan Temple records. The temple describes it as a six-story reinforced-concrete structure featuring elaborate dragon and phoenix decorations and a combination of southern and northern Chinese architectural styles.
Kao said the temple has announced a fundraising account through its official Facebook page and hopes public support will allow reconstruction to begin as quickly as possible. He said any surplus funds remaining after restoration will be used to support firefighters by helping improve firefighting equipment and training.
Kao also expressed concern for the firefighters who responded to the blaze and said he hopes to cooperate with the Taipei City Fire Department to support firefighters injured or killed in the line of duty. Kao said he deeply understands the hardships and risks involved in their work, per CNA.
Zhinan Temple, located in Taipei’s Wenshan District, is one of the city’s best-known Taoist religious centers. The temple complex is also a popular destination for visitors because of its mountain setting, proximity to the Maokong Gondola, and views of Taipei and surrounding areas.
Kao thanked the public for its concern following the fire and said the temple’s priority is to restore the damaged hall while creating a safer environment for worshippers. “We hope to provide everyone with a safe and secure place in the future,” he said.

Taiwan airlines’ long-haul fuel surcharge to rise to NT$2,670
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:25:13 UTC
18:25:13 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Fuel surcharges on international passenger flights operated by Taiwan-based airlines will rise Sept. 7 as aviation fuel prices increase.
The Civil Aviation Administration said in a press release that the surcharge for short-haul routes will increase to US$32.50 (NT$1,028) per passenger per flight segment, while the long-haul surcharge will rise to US$84.50. This marks the fifth adjustment this year and the second consecutive monthly increase, per Mirror Media.
The agency said state-owned CPC Corp.'s latest international aviation fuel price rose from US$147.57 to US$156.79 per barrel, moving the applicable surcharge level from the 12th to the 13th tier.
The short-haul rate applies to routes in Asia, excluding India and the Middle East, and will increase by about NT$79 per flight segment. The long-haul rate covers Europe, the Americas, Africa, Oceania, Antarctica, India, and the Middle East, and will rise by about NT$206 per segment.
The agency has used a floating fuel surcharge mechanism with Taiwan-based airlines since 2005, based on CPC’s posted international aviation fuel price. No surcharge is imposed when the price is below US$40 per barrel, while rates start at US$5 for short-haul routes and US$13 for long-haul routes when the price is from US$40 to below US$50.
For every additional US$10 increase in the fuel price, the surcharge rises by US$2.50 for short-haul routes and US$6.50 for long-haul routes. The agency said the system adjusts surcharges in line with changes in fuel costs.
To address consumer concerns and protect passenger rights, the agency has instructed airlines to provide information on the share of fuel costs in ticket prices and how surcharges are calculated. Travelers can check the latest surcharge details on individual airlines’ websites before purchasing tickets.
International oil prices have fluctuated sharply this year amid instability in the Middle East, with long-haul fuel surcharges peaking at US$117 in April, Mirror Media reported. They then fell in June and July as oil prices declined, with short-haul and long-haul surcharges dropping to US$27.50 and US$71.50, respectively, before rising again in August.

Despite all these challenges, India’s economy grew by 7.8 per cent,” Prasad said at a press conference in Delhi.

So, let’s talk about these fundamental issues. 80 per cent of this country depends on free ration. Is that what good GDP growth does for the country? That’s our question.”
Khera had earlier taken his criticism to X, arguing that a single quarter of strong GDP growth should not be treated as evidence of broad-based economic prosperity.“One quarter of 7.8% growth is not an economic spring. If India has truly "bloomed," why do rampant unemployment, leaked exam papers, and a crumbling education system define the ground reality? Why is the republic's prosperity not translating into the prosperity of its public? GDP measures national output - not jobs, not wages, not opportunity. If it measured any of those, the future of India's youth would not look so bleak. Modi can manage his headlines. For India's youth, the question remains the same as ever: Where are the jobs?”
At his press conference, Khera also questioned whether the strong GDP reading had resulted in tangible improvements in the cost of living and employment conditions.“On one hand, they say, "Look at the GDP of a single quarter and applaud." On the other, they say, "Don't buy gold, don't host lavish weddings." They themselves sit abroad while telling the country's citizens not to travel overseas and to save money. 80% of the population relies on free rations, but keep applauding... Regarding this 7.8% figure—what benefit is the country's largest sector, agriculture, deriving from it? The youth constitute the country's largest demographic; what benefit are they getting? Have their issues been resolved? Have milk prices dropped? Is there no longer a need for free rations? Have you rectified the employment situation to reverse the 45-year record low? The competing responses underline the political divide over how India's economic performance should be assessed. While the BJP has used the 7.8 per cent quarterly expansion to highlight India's relative resilience amid global disruptions, the Congress has focused on whether headline GDP growth is being reflected in employment, household incomes and opportunities for India's young population.

Recyclable airplanes developed by Swiss researchers
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:24:00 UTC
18:24:00 KST

Recyclable airplanes developed by Swiss researchers
Scientists in Switzerland are working to make airplanes recyclable. A newly developed composite material is intended to ensure that lightweight and robust components no longer inevitably end up in landfill or incinerators.
Materials used in the construction of planes or trains must be lightweight, robust and flame-retardant. Until now, however, such composite materials have not been recyclable. Researchers have now developed a material designed to combine these properties, the Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology (EMPA) announced on Tuesday.
The material developed is a multi-layered composite. A core made of a heat-resistant aramid honeycomb structure is sandwiched between layers of glass or carbon fibres. Epoxy resin is used as the binder. Such resins cannot normally be melted down or dissolved. As a result, composite materials of this kind often end up in landfill sites or are incinerated.
The EMPA researchers added a phosphorus-containing molecule to the epoxy resin. This additive not only makes the material flame-retardant but also enables it to be recycled. Once cured, the resin can be softened again under certain conditions and reshaped.
More
Making synthetic fuels: a Swiss scientist’s bid to decarbonise cars and planes
Recovering all components
The main aim of the project was the complete recycling of the composite material. Using a solvent and heat, the composite can be broken down into its constituent parts. This allows the aramid honeycomb structure and the glass or carbon fibres to be recovered.
According to the researchers, the new material meets current fire safety requirements and achieves almost the same mechanical properties as conventional epoxy resin.
The next step is to scale up the manufacturing and recycling processes. The EMPA research team is also investigating further potential applications for the plastic, such as in the energy sector and the construction industry.
The project was carried out in collaboration with the industrial partner Elantas and supported by Innosuisse.

U.S. Army orders $712.5 million worth of artillery fuzes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:20:54 UTC
18:20:54 KST

- The U.S. Army awarded Action Manufacturing Co. a contract worth up to $712.5 million to produce M739A1 artillery fuzes.
- The indefinite-delivery contract runs through August 31, 2031, with only one company submitting a bid.
An artillery shell won’t explode without one small part screwed into its nose or tail: the fuze. The U.S. Army just signed a $712.5 million contract to keep a steady supply of them coming.
Action Manufacturing Co., based in Bristol, Pennsylvania, won the contract to build, inspect, test, package and deliver M739A1 point detonating and delay fuzes. Only one company bid for the job. Army Contracting Command in Newark, New Jersey, is overseeing the deal, which runs through August 31, 2031.
An artillery shell by itself is basically dead weight, a heavy metal tube filled with explosive that does nothing until something triggers it. That trigger is the fuze. Without one, you don’t have a weapon, you have expensive scrap metal.
The M739A1 is a “point detonating/delay” fuze, which means it can be set two different ways depending on the target. Set to detonate on impact, it explodes the instant the shell hits something, useful against troops or equipment out in the open. Set to delay, it lets the shell punch through a roof, a bunker wall or several feet of dirt first, then explodes a fraction of a second later, deep inside whatever it just penetrated. That flexibility is why the Army buys these by the hundreds of thousands rather than relying on a single fixed design.
The contract is structured as an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity deal, which is standard practice for parts like this. Instead of committing to buy a fixed number of fuzes up front, the Army sets a ceiling price, in this case $712.5 million, and orders however many it actually needs over the life of the contract as demand comes up. Work locations and funding get sorted out order by order rather than all at once.
The Army hasn’t said how many fuzes it expects to actually buy under this ceiling, where the manufacturing work will happen beyond Action Manufacturing’s Bristol facility, or how this order fits into the broader push to rebuild American artillery ammunition stockpiles that have been drawn down by years of supporting Ukraine.

Annual global climate-related losses to reach $450 bln — FT
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:18:59 UTC
18:18:59 KST

LONDON, September 1. /TASS/. Annual global losses from climate change could reach $450 bln in a "typical year" in the coming years and rise even further in catastrophic years, the Financial Times (FT) reported, citing US analytics company Verisk Analytics (VA).
Two years ago, such losses from natural disasters, including damage to expanding infrastructure, totaled $320 bln, according to UN estimates. Meanwhile, new data from risk modeling company VA show that as much as 62% of global losses from natural disasters, averaging around $279 bln, are uninsured.
The rising losses reflect the growing impact of climate change. Against this backdrop, the insurance industry, faced with mounting losses from catastrophic risks, is covering an increasingly smaller share of the total estimated damage. Major insurers have also withdrawn entirely from some regions, declining to renew policies in areas facing growing risks.
The magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Myanmar in March 2025 caused an estimated $12 bln in damage, of which insurers covered less than $100 mln, according to Verisk Analytics. Losses from the July 2025 floods in Texas, which killed 130 people, were estimated at $1.1 bln, but most of the damage was uninsured.

Sánchez explained that the government must base its actions on verified facts and identified the distortion of a Supreme Court ruling regarding swimming migrants as a key factor amplified across social media platforms and criminal networks.
Sánchez specifically identified Russia, Israel, and international far-right groups as sources of fake news aimed at using migration to destabilize Spain and create divisions within Europe. However, he clarified that this activity does not necessarily indicate direct actions by the respective foreign governments and noted that the complete origin of the campaign remains under investigation.
Following the broadcast, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar publicly rejected the claims on social media. Sa'ar stated, "In his interview today with Cadena SER, he lied again, unexpectedly accusing Israel of spreading false information about the events in Ceuta.
Addressing the role of Spain's National Intelligence Center (CNI), Sánchez confirmed that intelligence reports were provided prior to the July 30 and 31 arrivals.
However, he stated that none of the documents foresaw the true scale of the situation. "CNI provided situation reports, but there was no information predicting the scale of the crisis we were going to experience," he explained.
Sánchez denied any contradiction between statements made by Defense Minister Margarita Robles, who noted that CNI shared intelligence regarding boundary crossings, and Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska, who stated there were no warnings of a mass entry of that magnitude.
The Spanish prime minister emphasized that security measures were heightened before the event based on available data, though the full extent could not be anticipated.
The prime minister explicitly ruled out any involvement by the Moroccan government, describing Rabat’s cooperation.
"Not one of the intelligence services with which the Spanish government regularly collaborates raises doubts about the involvement, in one way or another, of the Moroccan authorities," Sánchez stated. He emphasized that resolving the situation relies entirely on mutual trust and bilateral cooperation with Morocco.
Sánchez also announced that King Felipe VI will make his first official visit to Ceuta and Melilla after more than 12 years on the throne, with plans underway to expand local reception capacity to 6,000 spots.
The Spanish government plans to increase accommodation infrastructure in Ceuta to hold up to 6,000 individuals in the near future.
Previously, researchers documented a coordinated series of fabricated videos and fake media covers produced by a Russian-linked disinformation network, which falsely claimed that Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan was preparing for a military conflict with Russia.
Distributed across social media platforms by accounts associated with Kremlin influence operations, the campaign featured fabricated reports imitating legitimate media outlets, false allegations of secret agreements between Armenia and France, and personalized videos ordered from American actors via the Cameo platform to discourage support for Pashinyan ahead of elections.

Heylen Group snaps up Audi site in Vorst: 3,000 new jobs on the way at new business park

Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:18:35 UTC
18:18:35 KST

A buyer has been found for the former Audi car assembly plant in Vorst (Greater Brussels): the Heylen Group, a company based in the Kempen District is purchasing the site. It plans to develop a large business park, hosting local firms and international players. In the long term, the project is expected to create 3,000 jobs, roughly the same number as the jobs lost due to the closure of the Audi car assembly factory. A year and a half ago, the last car rolled off the production line at the Audi factory in Vorst. Since then, the site, covering some 55 hectares, has stood empty.
Heylen Group snaps up Audi site in Vorst: 3,000 new jobs on the way at new business park
For a long time, it was unclear what would become of Brussels’ largest industrial site. Among other possibilities, it was mooted as a potential defence site. That will not be happening after all.
Heylen Group comprises more than 40 companies and is owned by an entrepreneur from Herentals (Antwerp Province). Heylen aims to turn the site into “one of Brussels’ most dynamic economic centres”.
‘Rings Park 21’
The project has been named ‘Rings Park 21’. Dozens of businesses are set to move in, ranging from large to small players. Exactly which companies these will be is not yet clear. Part of the site is also set to be opened to the public. The nearby Vorst-Zuid railway station will also be integrated into the project.
‘Bringing together SMEs and established industrial activities is precisely the model of urban economy that we want to develop in Brussels,’ says Laurent Hublet, the Brussels Employment and Economy Minister (Francophone centrist Les Engagés). ‘This project is in line with that and ensures that the site continues to serve the Brussels economy and the people of Brussels.’
To attract entrepreneurs to the site, the minister has promised incentives, such as tax incentives and fast-track planning permission.
Employment recovery
‘Rings Park 21’ is expected to create at least 3,000 jobs – roughly the same number as the old Audi workforce. Heylen Warehouses aims to create these jobs as quickly as possible.
“We’re getting started straight away, because every day counts when it comes to employment. The urgency is not only financial but also social: the sooner this forward-looking project becomes operational, the sooner Brussels can restore the lost jobs and generate a new dynamic for growth,” says CEO Ralph Caspanni. The company expects it will take just under 10 years to roll out the entire project.
The purchase price has not been disclosed. In March, the group also acquired a large part of the former Caterpillar factory in Gosselies, near Charleroi (Hainault Province). There, 37.5 hectares are being redeveloped into an SME-zone.

Estonia's new expert panel to tackle online risks to youth mental health
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:18:00 UTC
18:18:00 KST

Estonia's new expert panel to tackle online risks to youth mental health
An expert panel convened by the Estonian government is examining online risks to youth mental health in a push for solutions to make digital spaces safer for kids and teens.
The panel will submit recommendations to the government by the end of 2026, covering measures for kids and teens, parents and guardians as well as the state that preserve the benefits of digital technology while reducing potential harms.
"Youths' anxiety and mental health issues are a serious and growing concern," said Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform). "Several countries have introduced or are considering restrictions on youths' social media use in recent years, but more crucial than bans are solutions that actually help our young people."
The panel's leading experts, he added, will work with researchers, youth workers and representatives of youth themselves to find effective ways to reduce the negative effects of social media.
Troubling studies
The move comes amid signs of growing problematic digital use among Estonian kids and teens.
A 2025 University of Tartu study found students were increasingly exposed to disturbing online content, sexually explicit messages and excessive internet use, with harmful content and cyberbullying also linked to poorer mental well-being.
A 2022 National Institute for Health Development (TAI) found symptoms of social media addiction among 8 percent of 11- to 15-year-olds, up from 6 percent in 2018.
The study also linked social media use with lower life satisfaction, less sleep, weaker school performance and more frequent depressive episodes.
The researchers stressed, however, that digital technology itself does not cause mental health issues, with its effects depending on how and why it is used.
Practical solutions, not blanket bans
The newly convened panel brings together experts in media studies, psychology, neuroscience, education, mental health, child protection and youth work, along with a youth representative. University of Tartu media studies professor Andra Siibak was elected panel chair.
"Our common goal is to develop multilevel solutions based on scientific research and international best practices and tailored to Estonia's circumstances and our young people's experiences," said Siibak.
"We will be working with young people to develop and discuss these solutions to ensure our recommendations are not only evidence-based but also genuinely workable for the target group they are meant to serve," she added.
The panel will examine risks associated with both social media and online video game platforms.
Its next meeting is scheduled for September 14.

Eurozone inflation hits highest since September 2023 as energy costs accelerate
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:16:22 UTC
18:16:22 KST

Mücahithan Avcıoğlu
01 September 2026•Update: 01 September 2026
Euro area annual inflation accelerated to 3.3% in August, its highest level since September 2023, when it stood at 4.3%, according to a flash estimate released by Eurostat on Tuesday.
The rate rose from 2.9% in July, remaining above the European Central Bank’s medium-term target of 2%.
Consumer prices increased 0.4% on a monthly basis in August, the EU’s statistical office said.
Energy was the main driver of the acceleration, with annual energy inflation climbing to 14.3% from 10.3% in July. Energy prices increased 2.9% month on month.
Annual inflation for non-energy industrial goods also rose to 1.2% from 0.9%.
In contrast, services inflation eased to 3% from 3.3%, while inflation for food, alcohol and tobacco remained unchanged at 1.2%.
Core inflation, which excludes energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, edged down to 2.4% from 2.5%. Inflation excluding only energy remained stable at 2.2%.
Among euro-area members, Lithuania recorded the highest annual inflation rate at 5.8%, followed by the Greek Cypriot Administration at 5.2% and Bulgaria at 5.1%.
Spain’s annual inflation climbed to 4.5%, while the rate stood at 4.2% in Belgium, 3.2% in Italy, 2.9% in Germany, and 2.7% in France.
The lowest annual rates were recorded in Estonia at 1.3%, Malta at 1.9%, and Finland at 2.4%.

Cigarettes are on the decline in the EU, but how popular are smoking and vaping still?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:13:26 UTC
18:13:26 KST

Despite the EU's goal of creating a "Tobacco-Free Generation" by 2040, more than 16% of people over 16 smoke and vape every single day. Who are the biggest smokers in the bloc?
It's well-known that smoking is harmful to your health, and the use of cigarettes in Europe is seeing a slow yet steady decline.
In 2025, one in six people aged 16 or older in the EU used tobacco and related products, such as e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches, every day, according to Eurostat.
The statistics office said that 20.8% of men smoked every day, compared with 12.6% of women.
However, both shares decreased slightly compared with 2022, when 22.2% of men and 13.1% of women smoked daily.
Tobacco kills 1.1 million people in Europe each year, with 153,000 of those dying from exposure to second-hand smoke, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
Furthermore, deaths from lung cancer attributable to tobacco use are 71% for men and 46% for women.
As tobacco is such a prevalent cause of cancer, the EU has brought in measures to stem its use, including a goal to reduce its use to less than 5% of the population by 2040 under its Beating Cancer Plan.
Tobacco use varies by age, although not significantly. People aged between 35 and 49 years old registered the highest share (21.3%) of daily users of tobacco, e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches, according to Eurostat.
This was followed by people aged between 25 and 34 at 19.9%, and those aged between 50 and 64 at 19.8%.
Which countries smoke the most?
Among EU countries, Bulgaria (26.3%), Sweden (23.9%) and Croatia (23.6%) recorded the highest shares of the daily use of tobacco and related products.
In contrast, the Netherlands (9.9%), Ireland (11.7%), Belgium (13.6%) and Luxembourg (13.8%) had the lowest shares.
In 17 EU countries, the share of people who used tobacco and related products daily decreased between 2022 and 2025.
The largest decreases were in Spain and Luxembourg, while Croatia and Lithuania recorded the largest increases.
Are citizens aware of the smoking consequences?
Despite years of tobacco-control policies, graphic warnings and public-health campaigns about the dangers of smoking, medical journal BMJ Open found that awareness of its health consequences has barely improved over the past two decades.
More than 90% of respondents knew that smoking can cause lung cancer.
Yet, only about 80% identified heart disease as a consequence of smoking and even fewer knew about the stroke risk as well as second-hand smoke risks.
Researchers found that awareness that smoking causes lung cancer increased significantly in the Netherlands in the same timeframe, but declined in countries such as Germany, France, and Romania.

Xi's visit to Egypt marks Chinese interest in Middle East, Egypt's push to keep growing - analysis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:12:26 UTC
18:12:26 KST

China’s President Xi Jinping is visiting Egypt on Tuesday for a three-day visit that underscores China’s continued interest in the Middle East. MBN News noted it is his first visit to Egypt since 2016, adding that "it coincides with the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Egypt was the first Arab and African state to establish relations with the People’s Republic of China in 1956.”
The report at MBN adds that “the anniversary offers both governments an opportunity to highlight a partnership that has expanded into infrastructure, trade, telecommunications, space technology, defense and artificial intelligence. Behind the official celebrations, however, is a more practical question: Why has Egypt become so important to China?”
Why indeed? Egypt is a large country with around 100 million people. It has the Suez Canal; it sits at the junction of the Middle East and North Africa; it plays a role in Libya and Sudan; and it has historically been a leader in the Arab world. Egypt was also an important country during the Cold War and has continued to be an anchor of the entire region.
However, instability during the Arab Spring and the rule of Mohammed Morsi left questions about what comes next. In recent years, Egypt has stabilized and also invested heavily in new military-security institutions.
China Daily noted that “in congratulatory messages exchanged on May 30 on the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between the two countries, President Xi Jinping said China-Egypt relations have become a model of amity, solidarity and cooperation among developing countries, as well as a benchmark for collective cooperation between China and Arab states and between China and Africa.”
China is keen to work with Egypt
The report says that Xi is keen to work with Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi. This can lead to a “push for the growth of China-Egypt relations featuring greater strategic guidance, stronger synergy for development and broader international influence.” China has been seeking greater inroads in the Middle East. It would like to see economic blocs such as BRICS and SCO expand their role in the region. However, it is cautious. It saw how a 25-year deal with Iran did not pan out. It is wary of the instability caused by the Iran conflict.
“Egyptian President El-Sisi said Egypt and China have stood shoulder to shoulder through different historical periods and that bilateral relations have maintained steady growth over the past 70 years. He expressed the hope of working with Xi to advance bilateral ties and jointly build a more stable multipolar world with a greater capacity to address global challenges,” China Daily notes.
The report goes on to note that “China and Egypt signed a memorandum of understanding on jointly building the Belt and Road in January 2016, when Xi made a state visit to Egypt. In 2024, the two countries signed a cooperation plan to further align the Belt and Road Initiative with Egypt's Vision 2030.” Chinese companies have played a role in “building the Central Business District in Egypt's new administrative capital and the 10th of Ramadan light rail transit system.”
Economic and trade initiatives are clear. “Tarek Nosseir, president of the Cairo-based think tank Global Forum for Future Studies, told Xinhua News Agency that Chinese participation in major projects had helped to localize advanced technologies, attract investment, support national development plans and create tens of thousands of jobs. He also pointed to collaboration in renewable energy, the national power grid and transportation networks,” China Daily added.
There is a lot of talk about how both countries are ancient civilizations. China feels comfortable placing its bets on a country like Egypt, which has such a long past. Egypt’s Ahram Online also said the same thing about how the countries have ancient civilizations.
It also noted that the visit coincides with the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. “Ambassador Ezzat Saad, executive director of the Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs (ECFA), said Egypt and China represent two of the oldest civilizations in human history,” Ahram noted, echoing the same message discipline being put forth in Cairo and Beijing. “This year also marks 10 years since Xi’s historic visit to Cairo, during which he delivered a major address at the headquarters of the Arab League and presented China’s policy towards the Arab world.”
The Ahram report added that “relations gained considerable momentum following President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi’s assumption of office in 2014, particularly because of his appreciation of China’s experience in achieving comprehensive and sustainable development. The two countries subsequently elevated their relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership.”
Egypt's relations with the BRICS group
BRICS also came up in the messaging. “Egypt began engaging with BRICS through the BRICS Plus framework in September 2017. China introduced the format during the BRICS summit in Xiamen, which El-Sisi attended at Xi’s invitation,” Ahram added.
“China has become one of Egypt’s most important economic partners, while Egypt provides Beijing with a strategically located gateway to Arab and African markets through its ports, transport networks and the Suez Canal. Egypt, in turn, benefits from Chinese investment, expertise and technology in infrastructure, energy, transport, telecommunications and industry.”
A few other details are worth noting, based on Egyptian government media coverage. Egypt’s Sisi has made eight trips to China. “Egypt’s Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade put bilateral trade at about $19.52 billion in 2025, describing China as one of Egypt’s largest trading partners.”
Additionally, Egypt has sought to increase exports to China. Chinese investment is believed to exceed $10 billion in Egypt, focusing on “construction, textiles, electronics, energy, transport, and industrial manufacturing.”
In addition, Ahram adds that “the China-Egypt TEDA Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone in Ain Sokhna is a central part of the relationship. A July 2025 agreement expanded the TEDA industrial zone from seven to about 10 square kilometers. The zone hosted 185 companies when Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited Egypt that month." Many projects are continuing, including manufacturing investments.

Kenya aviation workers end 2-day strike after deal with government
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:12:19 UTC
18:12:19 KST

Andrew Wasike 
01 September 2026•Update: 01 September 2026
Kenyan aviation workers on Tuesday called off a two-day strike that disrupted air traffic and caused flight cancellations and delays at major airports across the East African country after reaching a return-to-work agreement with the government and aviation authorities.
The Kenya Aviation Workers Union (KAWU) agreed to immediately end the industrial action after signing the deal with the Transport Ministry, Kenya Airports Authority (KAA), Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA) and Kenyan carrier Jambojet.
“The employees shall resume their respective duties and cooperate with management to ensure the immediate restoration and continuity of normal operations,” the agreement said.
Under the deal, agency fees owed to KAWU and held by KAA will be released to the union immediately.
KAWU and KCAA will also resume negotiations on a collective bargaining agreement, with KCAA committing to honor and implement the outcome.
The agreement also states that workers who participated in the strike will not be victimized, intimidated, discriminated against or subjected to disciplinary action over their involvement.
A separate dispute between KAWU and Jambojet over recognition of the union remains before the courts, with both sides agreeing to abide by the eventual ruling.
The strike began Sunday and disrupted operations at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) in Nairobi, as well as airports in Mombasa, Kisumu and Eldoret.
Kenya Airways said some of its flights were canceled, delayed or otherwise disrupted, while RwandAir canceled its WB452 and WB453 services Monday due to air traffic control constraints at JKIA.
It was the second major aviation workers’ strike in Kenya this year.
In February, KAWU members staged another strike that disrupted Kenyan airspace and operations at JKIA for about a day and a half before returning to work following government-mediated talks.

IDF conducts strikes across Gaza Strip amid reports of attempted kidnapping of Hamas official
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:12:08 UTC
18:12:08 KST

Defense Minister Israel Katz on Tuesday confirmed that the IDF had successfully captured a senior Hamas terrorist while carrying out strikes on several targets in the Gaza Strip in response to threats against Israeli forces.
An Israeli official told The Jerusalem Post that the terrorist who was captured is Hamas's Head of General Security Apparatus.
"A short time ago, a senior Hamas terrorist was arrested, and this is our policy: We do not wait for threats. Instead, we pursue Hamas terrorists, thwart them, and destroy their terrorist infrastructure. We have built a strong and unprecedented security zone in Gaza to protect residents and IDF soldiers," Katz said.
"Nearly 70% of the Gaza Strip has been destroyed, with no residents, no tunnels, and no homes, and the IDF controls the territory. We are not leaving Gaza until the Strip is demilitarized, Hamas is disarmed, and all terrorist tunnels are destroyed. Even after that, the IDF will remain in Gaza along defensive lines and ensure the security of the western Negev communities. Any attempt to bypass the security zone through aerial launches will be met with a harsh response."
It was unclear what strategic change could be achieved in the standoff with Hamas through the operation, though its daring and the entrance of Israeli-aligned forces deeper into a Hamas area were bound to grab the public's attention mid-election more than the regular airstrikes, which barely register in the media most days.
Following the strikes, the IDF stated that there had been no Israeli casualties.
Initially, Al Hadath reported that the IDF had coordinated with Gazan militias to attempt to "kidnap a figure near the Red Cross headquarters in Gaza."
According to Al Hadath, the strikes occured after the operation was exposed.
IDF sources would not deny foreign reports that Israel worked alongside Gazan militias to arrest the senior Hamas official.
However, on the record, the IDF only referred to its extremely vague statement about removing Hamas threats.
Ten explosions were heard in the Gaza City area as a result of the strikes, Palestinian sources reported. Al Jazeera reported that Israeli military aircraft were flying at low altitude over the area, while Al Hadath reported that drones continued to drop a large number of bombs in the area.
IDF special forces reportedly entered American Hospital area
Additionally, reports emerged that IDF special forces had entered the area of the American Hospital in the al-Katiba area of western Gaza City.
Palestinian reports described exchanges of fire and shooting involving special forces in western Gaza City. There were also reports of a large number of casualties among Gazans as a result of the strikes.
Separately, there were reports of smoke shells being fired in the Shati refugee camp in western Gaza City, along the coast.
Local gangs contribute, but are not primary drivers of toppling Hamas
Political leaks suggesting that Gaza's local gangs have any chance of taking over Gaza from Hamas in the near or medium term are divorced from reality.
Each of these groups can only survive now with clear IDF protection and can only confront Hamas for small and limited operations.
If their numbers range between the dozens and a couple of hundred, Hamas still has thousands or more foot soldiers.
Put differently, these local gangs might contribute over the long term to Hamas's fall, but they will not be a central component of it.
Rather, most experts agree that either some arm of the Palestinian Authority or a hybrid of the PA, Egypt, the ISF, and some outside IDF support would be needed to overcome Hamas in the long term.
Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

Montenegro manhunt ends with Russian triple-murder suspect dead, police say
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:11:10 UTC
18:11:10 KST

According to the interior ministry, the suspect, a 30-year-old Russian, shot dead three employees of a shooting range in Danilovgrad, close to the capital Podgorica.
A police search for an armed Russian man in Montenegro ended early on Tuesday when the suspect, wanted for killing three people, killed himself after exchanging fire with police, authorities said.
According to the interior ministry, the suspect, a 30-year-old Russian, shot dead three employees of a shooting range in Danilovgrad, close to the capital Podgorica.
After an hours-long manhunt involving special units and a helicopter, the suspect was located in woods above the popular coastal tourist town of Herceg Novi, more than 120 kilometres from the crime scene.
"After the suspect was surrounded and found himself with no way out, he opened fire on police officers before killing himself with a firearm," police said in a statement.
The victims were two men from Podgorica, aged 20 and 24, and a 67-year-old man from Danilovgrad. The suspect fled the scene in a vehicle belonging to one of the victims.
No further details of the killings in Danilovgrad were released.
"Police are continuing their investigation with the Higher State Prosecutor’s Office in Podgorica to establish all the circumstances of the incident, including its cause and motive," police said.
Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajić expressed condolences to the victims’ families and announced two days of national mourning from Tuesday.

Call to prevent conflicts, not using finance as weapon: Putin’s statements
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:09:12 UTC
18:09:12 KST

BISHKEK, September 1. /TASS/. Countries must do everything possible to prevent the provocation of armed conflicts in global practice, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).
He also noted that the SCO Development Bank should be as independent as possible from the financial systems of countries that use finance as a weapon.
TASS has compiled the Russian leader’s key statements.
Call to prevent provocation of conflicts
Countries must do everything possible to prevent the provocation of armed conflicts in global practice: "I would like to remind you that today is September 1. This is the day World War II began. We must do everything possible to eliminate any provocation of armed conflicts. I am convinced that our work is precisely leading us in that direction."
Finance as weapon
The SCO Development Bank should be as independent as possible from the financial systems of countries that use finance as a weapon: "[The SCO Development Bank], in my opinion, should be as independent as possible from the financial systems of those states that use economic instruments as a weapon to gain unilateral advantages in international affairs."
In the future, the bank could contribute significantly to the implementation of joint, mutually beneficial economic projects, similar to the Business Council and the Interbank Association.
SCO development and role
In the 25 years since its establishment, the SCO has "come a truly long way."
Russia’s trade turnover with the SCO countries exceeded $400 billion last year.
The share of national currencies in mutual settlements between Russia and SCO member states exceeds 98%: "National currencies are being used more and more in transactions between our countries. In Russia's transactions with SCO members, national currencies account for over 98%."
In the 25 years since its creation, the SCO has become one of the independent and influential centers of the emerging multipolar world: "Let me remind you that, established in 2001 on the initiative of six states - Russia, China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan - it has grown stronger and expanded, becoming one of the independent and influential centers of the emerging multipolar world."
The member states actively cooperate in a variety of areas, contributing to each member state's development: "The SCO members actively cooperate in the political, economic, and humanitarian spheres. Such cooperation ensures the systematic and sustainable development of each state and contributes to an atmosphere of peace, stability, trust, and cooperation across our shared Eurasian continent."
Strengthening commercial ties among SCO member states brings them clear benefits: "Among the pressing practical tasks facing the SCO, I would like to highlight the further strengthening of commercial ties among member states. This brings clear benefits to all of us and genuinely contributes to steady socioeconomic growth and improved public welfare."
SCO members must act in a coordinated manner in the energy sector and maintain a balanced policy: "I believe it is in our common interest to continue a coordinated and balanced energy policy as outlined in the SCO's Energy Cooperation Strategy through 2030."
World Nomad Games
Russia is ready to host the 7th World Nomad Games in Kazan in 2028: "Our country is ready to host the next edition of these games in 2028 in Kazan. We look forward to welcoming teams from interested countries."

In Romania and the Baltic countries, alerts were declared overnight and fighter jets were scrambled
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
12:08:32 EEST
18:08:32 KST

In Romania and the Baltic countries, alerts were announced at night and fighter jets were scrambled
Kyiv • UNN
Air raid alerts were announced in Romania, Estonia and Latvia because of drones. NATO fighter jets were scrambled for monitoring; no incursion into Romania was recorded.
In Romania and two Baltic countries, an alert was declared overnight and fighter jets were scrambled, UNN reports, citing Romania’s Ministry of Defense and ERR.
Details
According to Romania’s Ministry of Defense, "the radar surveillance system of the Ministry of National Defense detected two aerial targets at 11:30 p.m. on Monday, August 31, 24 km northeast of Vylkove, Ukraine, near the border with Romania."
"Two F-18 aircraft of the Spanish Aerospace Force, serving as part of the Enhanced Air Policing mission at the 57th Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base, took off to monitor the situation at 11:43 p.m. At 12:05 a.m., an IAR-330 PUMA SOCAT helicopter of the Romanian Air Force was also scrambled," the statement said.
As noted, the population was alerted, and at 11:56 p.m. a RO-Alert message was sent, covering the northeastern part of Tulcea County.
"The pilots reported explosions on the territory of Ukraine. No intrusion into national airspace was reported. The air raid alert ended at 1:15 a.m.," Romania’s Ministry of Defense said.
According to ERR, during the night of September 1, the Estonian Defence Forces also sent warnings of a possible air threat, initially to residents of two counties and then to six more counties. The alert was canceled shortly before 6 a.m.
According to the military, several drones entered Estonian airspace. Turkish fighter jets participating in the NATO mission to patrol the airspace of the Baltic countries were scrambled to search for them, ERR reported.
Residents of two counties received the first threat notification at around 3:11 a.m. local time. Some received the information slightly later. At 3:48 a.m., the warning was extended to six more counties.
Colonel Uku Arold, head of the Strategic Communications Department of the Estonian Defence Forces, said that the military had detected drones moving along the eastern border of Estonia and Latvia, some of which had entered Estonian airspace.
"Drones were detected moving parallel to Estonia’s eastern border, as well as Latvia’s eastern border, and they entered Estonian territory, so we also declared an alert," Arold said.
According to him, Turkish fighter jets participating in the NATO mission to patrol Baltic airspace were scrambled in response to the threat.
On Tuesday night, a warning of a possible threat from the air was also declared in Latvia.
At around 2:00 a.m., residents of Ludza Municipality received the message, and at 2:25 a.m. the Latvian military reported that the warning had been canceled. Later, at 3:37 a.m., a threat was declared in Alūksne Municipality.
In response to the threat, NATO fighter jets patrolling the airspace of the Baltic countries were activated. At around 4:20 a.m., the Latvian authorities reported that the threat in Alūksne Municipality had passed. Meanwhile, the fighter jets continued searching for drones, now over Estonian territory.
Latvia has already encountered drones several times this year. In June and August, NATO fighter jets shot down drones that had entered the country’s airspace on two occasions.
The Finnish Defence Forces again restricted traffic in the eastern part of the Gulf of Finland.
"A temporary restriction zone for aviation and shipping was introduced in the eastern part of the Gulf of Finland early Tuesday morning," the Finnish Defence Forces said on social media. According to the military, the measure was preventive and intended to ensure the safety of third parties, as well as create conditions for the authorities to operate if it became necessary to counter possible drones.
In recent weeks, air and maritime traffic in the eastern part of the Gulf of Finland has already been restricted several times.
Estonian authorities note that, amid Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, there is a possibility that drones could deviate from their course and enter Estonian airspace.

One of 43 Australians reported missing in the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster has been found alive in Tibet.
The person is receiving support from Australian consular officers and has spoken with family members.
What's next?
More than 4,400 people remain missing across the affected areas, with search and rescue efforts continuing along the Nepal-China border.
One of 43 missing Australians has been found alive six days after catastrophic floods hit the Nepal-China border.
In a statement, the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said it was unable to provide details about the person due to privacy obligations.
The Australian was in Tibet, China.
"It's hard to imagine the sense of relief their loved ones must be feeling after what will have been an incredibly harrowing few days," Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong said in a statement on Tuesday.
More than 4,400people remain missing in the affected area.
The rescue effort comes after the "golden window" of the first 72 hours for finding a survivor, which experts say offers the best chances of survival without access to clean water.
The Australian has spoken with their family and is receiving support from consular officers.
Another Australian, Cara Severino, was safely located on the weekend, bringing the number of Australians missing following the flash floods down to 42.
Despite the welcome news, the Foreign Affairs Minister warned that the government "must remain realistic about the days ahead".
"As each day passes, our grave concerns for those still unaccounted-for inevitably grow," she said.
China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) did not provide further details when asked about the missing Australian found alive today.
MOFA said it was maintaining close communication with foreign embassies to jointly conduct investigations into missing foreign nationals.
Yesterday, the Australian government announced it would increase its humanitarian assistance for Nepal to $8 million.
Assistant Foreign Minister Matt Thistlewaite said this funding would mostly go towards the supply of hygiene kits.
"There's a desperate need for these kits for people in the region and also solar lights," he said.
"Obviously all of the power and telecommunications infrastructure has been wiped out.
"So those kits are being put together; they'll be transported by the Australian Defence Force over the coming days."

French rail start-up Velvet gets green light to compete with SNCF on high-speed lines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
09:05:25 UTC
18:05:25 KST

A new French rail company has secured the first approval needed to launch high-speed services from Paris to cities including Bordeaux, Nantes and Angers, potentially bringing more choice and competition to some of the country’s busiest routes.
France’s high-speed rail network could soon have a new name on departure boards, as a homegrown start-up prepares to take on state-owned SNCF.
Velvet, founded by a former SNCF executive, says it has secured an initial licence to operate high-speed trains on routes linking Paris with cities including Bordeaux, Nantes and Angers, with services planned from 2028.
On its website, the company says it wants to add 10 million seats between Paris and destinations along France’s Atlantic coast, with direct journeys averaging around two hours.
For travellers, that could mean more choice – and potentially more competitive fares – on some of the country’s busiest rail routes.
Although it has successfully obtained a first approval from the French transport ministry, Velvet now needs to secure a safety certification from France’s rail regulator before it can launch.
The French passenger rail market was opened to competition in 2020, as part of EU market liberalisation efforts, but SNCF remains by far the dominant operator.
Velvet is one of several challengers hoping to change that, alongside French start-up Le Train, Spain’s Renfe and Italy’s Trenitalia. The latter also plans to compete with Eurostar on the Paris-to-London service.
Rachel Picard, Velvet’s president and a former SNCF executive, said the new licence was “an important step” towards preparing its trains, staff and operations.
The company has raised €1 billion from a French investment fund, much of which will go towards buying 12 Avelia Horizon trains from Alstom – the same next-generation trains SNCF is also introducing.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party on Tuesday withdrew its call for a march on September 5 after Supreme Court, on the Centre's request, quashed all FIRs registered across the country against students who participated in the NEET protests."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.This comes after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, informed the apex court that the Centre remains committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to the leadership of CJP during the meeting between the Centre and the party.
What were the three assurances
The first assurance was that the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25.The second assurance was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would pay compensation to students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."Centre is committed to honour the assurance given to the CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after NEET exam cancellation; however, 3 months needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told SC.
"As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Earlier on Monday, Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIR's registered against the student protesters with alleged violence during protests over the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned the plea before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday, seeking the court’s intervention in the matter.The Centre has urged the Supreme Court to exercise its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the FIRs registered against the protesting students.
Why CJP had called for Sept 5 march
CJP had called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5, Teachers' Day. It had accused the Centre of failing to honour the promises made on July 25 to persuade the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation against irregularities in exams and the NEET paper leak.
According to the CJP, the march was to be led by families of students who committed suicide following the cancellation of the NEET exam and the subsequent re-test, as well as those who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July agitation.

European Peace Facility funds could become available to Ukraine – Kallas
EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas said this while speaking to reporters today before the start of an informal meeting of EU defense ministers in Ireland, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
Asked whether Ukraine could expect any concrete results from today’s meeting of defense ministers, Kallas noted that the informal nature of the meeting did not provide for any decisions to be taken, while adding that discussions would include efforts to unblock European Peace Facility funds.
“We will not take any decisions directly, but we are indeed working to unblock the European Peace Facility,” she said.
It should be recalled that €6.6 billion available under the European Peace Facility instrument remains blocked as member states continue discussions over the mechanism for distributing the funds.
“If this happens in the coming days, many member states have already said that all the funds they receive back [for defense spending already incurred – Ed.] will be provided to Ukraine. So this would also mean significant additional funding for air defenses and the weapons Ukraine needs,” she said.

Kyiv • UNN
Russia is preparing pseudo-elections in the occupied territories on September 20. More than 300 million rubles have been allocated for them in Donetsk region alone.
The Russian authorities are once again preparing to stage an electoral spectacle in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine on September 20 - on the "single voting day," when elections to the State Duma will also be held. This time, it will cost them hundreds of millions of rubles, reports the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine, according to UNN.
Details
The scenario remains unchanged. The first is to strengthen control over the sentiments of residents in the five temporarily occupied regions. The second goal is much more prosaic: elections have become a convenient pretext for appropriating budget funds by both Russians and local collaborators. In the temporarily occupied part of Donetsk region alone, more than 300 million rubles were allocated from the budget of the "DPR" to hold the elections, against the backdrop of an acute socioeconomic crisis in these territories

01 September 2026•Update: 01 September 2026
Germany’s government intends to hold Russia responsible for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig Airport following investigators’ findings, the daily Bild reported Tuesday.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has changed his travel plans so he could appear with Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt at a news conference later on Tuesday, the newspaper reported, citing security sources.
Bild said the government now assumes the Leipzig incident was an attack attempt commissioned by Moscow. Berlin had so far held back from a direct public attribution. Until now, Dobrindt had spoken only of “foreign powers” behind the incident.
According to the security sources, the trail from the explosive-laden drone points to a Russian intelligence service. Investigators’ findings have “condensed to the point” that Berlin wants to attribute the case to that service, Bild reported.
German authorities told media last week that the attempted attack on a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane at Leipzig Airport in August was more serious than initially described. The drone had been rigged with explosives, and investigators have concluded that several drones were involved rather than one.
Welt am Sonntag also reported that the discovery of a weapons cache near Berlin has hardened the German government’s stance. Germany’s domestic intelligence agency, the BfV, assessed that the weapons were stashed for Russian spies who could be ordered by Moscow to carry out assassinations.
The Russian Embassy in Berlin has not issued an official statement on the allegations. Moscow has previously rejected claims of assassinations, sabotage and spying in countries allied with Ukraine, accusing Western governments of stoking “anti-Russian paranoia.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tueday said an Indian national was among those killed in the latest overnight Russian attacks, adding a new dimension to the strikes just a day after Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.
Russia launched a large aerial attack in and around Ukraine’s capital overnight into Tuesday morning, killing at least 12 people and wounding more than a dozen others, including three children, local authorities said.
Zelenskyy said the death underscored the human cost of Russia's war in Ukraine and called for the violence to end. Modi, during his meeting with Putin on Monday, had said there was no solution to the Ukraine conflict on the battlefield and that the war must end "for humanity's sake", according to a readout of the meeting.
Ukraine’s air force said that Russia began the attack at 6 pm on Monday (1500 GMT), using ballistic, cruise and anti-radar missiles, as well as 218 drones and decoys. About a third of the drones were reportedly jet-powered.
The main targets were the Kiev and Odessa regions, the air force said in a statement on Telegram.
The overnight strikes marked the sixth consecutive day of Russian attacks on Kiev, following a stretch of air raid alerts that began last week.
The latest attack struck civilian infrastructure and residential buildings in several districts of Kiev, with eight people killed in the city itself and three others in the surrounding region.
The death toll
The Russian strikes killed seven people in the Darnytskyy district of the capital, authorities said. One person was seriously wounded and hospitalised, the emergency service said. At another site in the district, an explosion wounded two people, including a child.
An eighth person was killed in the Holosiivskyy district, when a nonresidential building was hit and caught fire, the emergency service said in a statement. In the Solomianskyy district, a drone strike hit a residential building, causing damage. Emergency workers rescued a man and freed a woman trapped beneath the rubble.
The other three people who died were in areas of the Kiev region outside the city, and 12 were wounded. In Boryspil, three cars caught fire.
Emergency crews evacuated 48 people and rescued two from under the rubble. Eight people were injured, including two children. Also in Boryspil, a truck caught fire at an infrastructure facility, damaging the building. Two people were killed and three others injured, the emergency service said. A service station in Boryspil was also damaged, killing one person.
The Odessa region came under a major Russian attack overnight, damaging civilian infrastructure and wounding one person, regional head Oleh Kiper said.
Two residential buildings were damaged, while a fire broke out at a sewing factory. Russian forces also struck the Orlivka international ferry crossing on the border with Romania, he said.
Ukrainian forces said they destroyed or suppressed 199 aerial targets, including five ballistic missiles and 187 drones. Missile and drone strikes were recorded at 28 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at another 10 sites, it said.
Russia says attack targeted military-industrial and fuel and energy facilities
Russia's defence ministry, meanwhile, said its forces had carried out a "massive strike" using long-range weapons and attack drones.
It said the attack targeted military-industrial and fuel and energy facilities in Kiev and the surrounding region.
The ministry also said it had struck infrastructure in the southern Odessa region and the ports of Odessa and Chornomorsk.
Both sides have escalated long-range strikes in recent months, targeting infrastructure such as warehouses, businesses, and oil and port facilities, as well as ships, increasing civilian casualties.
Ukraine faces a shortage of interceptor missiles, particularly US-made Patriot systems used against ballistic threats.

China launches new academic journal for open sharing of scientific research data
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-01
17:02:11 CST
18:02:11 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 1 (Xinhua) -- The Institute of Automation under the Chinese Academy of Sciences recently launched an international academic journal titled Data Research and Applications (DRA), which is dedicated to the open sharing of scientific research data.
Data journals are of great significance in promoting the open sharing of scientific data, improving data governance and invigorating new paradigms in scientific research. This new journal has been established to provide a high-level interdisciplinary, open access and peer-reviewed academic exchange platform for researchers worldwide, said the institute.
The journal features six sections: data papers, model papers, research papers, reviews, data and model updates, as well as news opinions and comments.
Its scope spans multiple disciplines, including computer science, mathematics, statistics and medicine, encompassing the complete lifecycle of research output from generation to publication and iterative updates.
According to the institute, Data Research and Applications is a journal committed to building a complete chain linking data, research, application and governance, so as to promote the global open sharing of high-quality data resources.
The inaugural editorial board of this new journal brings together authoritative experts from over 20 renowned universities and research institutions worldwide, the institute noted. ■
